extracted.intended_audience: readers of early-modern English essays; students of literature and moral character studies
extracted.subtask_description: Short, moralizing character sketches describing types of people (e.g., 'A Baker', 'A Modest Man'), each listing traits, behaviours, and social consequences; useful as models for portraying or diagnosing human character in essays or fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Baker
rubrics_metrics.description: A baker who treats punishment as almsgiving, abhors charity and justice for fear of losing bread profits; his basket (goods) may be seized but he dislikes pillory and public disgrace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes mercenary, stingy behaviour: regards charity as wasted bread, dislikes market clerk, finds mercy in offenses because only his basket is taken; anti-pattern: giving alms considered waste; social consequence: punished with dole and pillory feared.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Pretender to Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: A scholar-mountebank who pretends to learning to make others look foolish, displays the appearance and accoutrements of scholarship but lacks real study or understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traits include: appears in slippers with pen in ear, libraries open to same page for years, carries Classical folios unread, quotes Seneca/Tacitus superficially, collects author names from catalogues/dedications, uses scraps of tavern wit and plagiarises; anti-pattern: valuing the opinion of learning over actual study; example behaviours: reading in fields with book before his face, attending sermons to brag about authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Herald
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of honor and pedigree who trades in heraldry, selling arms and pedigrees cheaply and sometimes corruptly, skilled in naming gentry but offering costly, worthless goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depicts the herald as pedlar of scutchions, pennons, and painted boar's heads; metaphorically 'fathers' many children onto gentry names; regional note: nature more hereditary in Wales; anti-pattern: charging high for trinket heraldry and equating French valuation with English worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Common Singing-Men in Cathedral Churches
rubrics_metrics.description: Choir men who sing well in church but drink and carouse, mixing religious service with tavern pastime; their learning is superficial and their conduct often disorderly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: they are 'eight parts of speech' of service, sing like bells but make a peal not concert; pray and drink as recreation, learn chapters before they read them, miscall Hebrew names, handle scripture superficially and pollute gospel with poor conversation and thumbs; external signs: gowns laced with ale; social outcome: often die in God's service and have wine/cakes at funeral.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Shop-keeper
rubrics_metrics.description: A noisy, talkative shopkeeper who boasts and over-sells, repeats the same wares to all customers, uses religious professions selectively, and is servile to those who pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behaviours: utters much though sells little, praises every item as best in town, tells rote lies, adapts religion to customers, treats favor as reason for tyranny; anti-pattern: professed honesty used as cover; social dynamic: behaves as slave to paying customer but tyrant to friends.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Blunt Man
rubrics_metrics.description: A plain-spoken, coarse fellow whose wit is sharper than his manners; hates ceremony, cuts to the point, and is suspicious of smooth courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traits: despises prefaces, uses old oaths, is touchy and quick to anger, speaks plainly and may assault the guilty with fists; positive: his jests suit his nature and often succeed; negative: counterfeit bluntness is dangerous because it disguises craft as frankness; social effect: considered honest and may suffer imprisonment for public grumbling.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Handsome Hostess
rubrics_metrics.description: An inn's attractive hostess whose charm increases tavern expenses; she may be familiar without distaste but is distrusted locally, and her attentions are an expensive part of lodging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions as the loadstone of the inn attracting gallants; her company is billed, contributes to greater consumption of sack, and her perceived honesty is often doubted by parish; example: her little jugs excuse a kiss and increase the reckoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Critic
rubrics_metrics.description: An antiquarian textual surgeon who delights in emending and annotating old authors, makes learning of orthography and fragments, and prides himself on restoring and castigating the dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behaviours: converses in fragments and Latinisms, identifies genuine vs. corrupted texts, swells editions with comments, uses archaic phraseology; social function: he 'makes all books sell dearer' by his editorial additions; anti-pattern: excessive vexation of authors long dead.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Sergeant, or Catch-pole
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector/arresting officer feared as a judgment; ambushes debtors, seizes persons in cowardly fashion, making streets feel more dangerous and inspiring hatred of authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depicts him as creditor's hawk, manacles as his hands, ambush in shop-stalls or lanes, respires men only in tavern, and is a mobile prison; social consequence: fosters disloyal thoughts and resentment toward the king's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: An University Dun
rubrics_metrics.description: A petty creditor who follows gentlemen for small debts, waits in stairways, plagues chambers, and runs long scores at butleries, being often instigator of study by his demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features: hired follower for ten shillings, persistent attendance, complains of ingratitude, frequents buttery to 'run you up a long score', influenced by beer and rhetoric; social effect: causes students to study by annoyance and is largely unsuccessful as a gallant.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Stayed Man
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplined, methodical man who orders himself, restrains passions, foresees consequences, lives within means, and balances action and leisure with measured temperament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive rubric for steadiness: squares expenses to coffers, acts with forethought, speaks sparingly but effectively, is temperate in passions, neither extravagant nor miserlily attached to fashions; social roles: respectful to superiors, plain to friends, good husband/father/master; anti-pattern: not given to making verses—more wisdom than wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Modest Man
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who undervalues himself, shrinks from applause, is easily ashamed by praise, learns willingly, and avoids high ambition for fear of discredit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traits: confutes commenders, fears expectation, sneaks from good actions, readily acknowledges errors, prefers learning to boast, is sensitive to ill tongue, aims mainly to avoid discredit rather than to seek reputation; social impact: limited ambition, hard to persuade into great offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Meer Empty Wit
rubrics_metrics.description: A person of ephemeral, flash-in-the-pan wit without learning: produces occasional conceits but lacks sustaining intellectual fuel, so talents quickly fade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics: bursts of bubble-like jokes, performs best in immediate improvisation but poor at sustained meditation; reads Martial as crutch, mainly good for company when idle; anti-pattern: wit without study leads to eventual oblivion.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Drunkard
rubrics_metrics.description: One who relinquishes reason to drink, becoming vulnerable, disordered, and careless of credit and business; his passions and vanities are exposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image: likened to Cham's seeing his father, an 'uncovered man'; body becomes 'miry way', limbs out of office, blind with eyes; social effect: harms self and friends, causes melancholy or renewed drinking, loses capacity for serious thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Prison
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrayed as the 'grave of the living' where inmates are shut from the world, hardened by shared misery, and where habits and language grow coarse and bitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive rubric about institutional effects: the prison breeds meagre looks, lice, tobacco, hardens or desensitizes inmates, fosters common complaint against lawyers, and becomes a late and dangerous school of wisdom—the company often worse for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Serving Man
rubrics_metrics.description: A gentleman's attendant who mirrors his master in fashion and behaviour, often dull-witted but serviceable, taking on the master's vices and privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics: follows master's steps, imitates cut and pleasures, may swagger in ale-houses with hawking terms, keeps best company in appearance only, and marriage under master's direction is his best service; social note: handsome for credit more than wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: An Insolent Man
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly elevated person who displays arrogance and distance, constantly marking his office and expecting deference; intolerably proud and offensive despite little merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs: uses place as concluding remark, treats acquaintances surlily, snaps at others, performs courtesies with imputation, makes preferment a shield for contempt; social outcome: engenders general hostility and becomes subject of ridicule when fallen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquaintance
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary stage of friendship — a lighter, common relation that may or may not grow into intimacy; acquaintance is the hoard from which friendship is chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains social gradient: acquaintance easily formed by presence, lacks depth of friendship which requires knowledge of faults and fears; notes on stability: place/country ties are weakest; best judgment sometimes from acquaintances as they are less partial than friends/enemies.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Meer Complimental Man
rubrics_metrics.description: A person composed of polite, fashionable phrases who promises generally but performs little; lies for good manners and cannot be trusted to particular acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traits: universal offers with exceptions, promises as mannerly words, gives satisfaction in first encounters but lacks substance, deceives with politeness; anti-pattern: confusing spoken courtesy with genuine commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Poor Fiddler
rubrics_metrics.description: A fiddler living on meagre earnings and charity, travelling to feasts and fairs, whose art gains small living and whose devotion to merry, often bawdy songs defines him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrait: 'so many strings above a beggar', relies on charity and tapsters, follows Christmas and country weddings, hates Puritans, and alternates between mirth and drunkenness; social role: provides entertainment but lives in poverty.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Meddling Man
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone who interferes in others' business though having none of his own; busy in appearance, presumes on plots, takes over tasks and does them poorly while obliging gratitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behaviours: thrusts into employments unsought, snatches others' work, offers impossible plans with serious demeanor, lays obligations upon those he 'helps', and often is unthanked; anti-pattern: busybody who hinders rather than helps.
